solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Faulty driver steers this golf shot deficiently

parts.note: the Ford Ka is a small car, something a driver steers

indicators.note: done deficiently, the golf stroke falls short by its final letter

parts.note: a putt is a gentle golf shot on the green

explanation.surface: A golfer blames a faulty driver club for steering a weak shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' looks like a golf club, but it is a motorist, and the thing steered is the Ford Ka car. 'Deficiently' cuts PUTT to PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: something broken or not working is said to have gone kaput.

clue.text: Legendary figure left Chelsea manager overlooking tense international

indicators.note: overlooking here means leaving out, so two letters are dropped from the manager's name

parts.note: Carlo Ancelotti managed Chelsea football club from 2009 to 2011
T abbreviates tense in grammar

explanation.surface: A football manager's office overlooks a tense international match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' reads as a view, but it means ignoring: one T and the final I go from ANCELOTTI, leaving ANCELOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the Arthurian knight of the Round Table, a figure of legend.

clue.text: Tom pinches road warning sign

indicators.note: pinching something means holding it tightly, so one word grips the other inside it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
Ave is the abbreviation for avenue, a kind of road

explanation.surface: Someone called Tom steals a road sign that warns motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a man's name; here it is a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a cautionary note or proviso, a signal to beware.

clue.text: Domino originally stained underneath stout

indicators.note: in a down entry, underneath puts the letter below the previous piece

parts.note: stout means fat

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word stained

explanation.surface: A domino tile has been stained underneath by spilt stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Domino is not the game piece but the singer Fats Domino.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats Domino was the American rock and roll pianist and singer; this is his forename.

clue.text: Checked wickerwork (top half should be twisted)

indicators.note: only the first three of the six letters are turned round, as top half in a down entry

parts.note: rattan is the cane used for wickerwork furniture

explanation.surface: Instructions for weaving a basket with a check pattern, twisting the top half.
explanation.walkthrough: The top half RAT becomes TAR, leaving TAN unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is cloth woven in a pattern of crossing stripes, a checked design, used as an adjective.

clue.text: Stinging creature around Orient, released thorn in one's side

indicators.note: around tells us the insect's letters go round the rest

parts.note: a bee is an insect with a sting

indicators.note: released means freed from order, so the letters of Orient are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A stinging insect let loose in the East becomes a constant irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: Orient looks like the East, but 'released' frees its letters to be rearranged; the insect's letters then wrap that new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: French for black beast, a bête noire is a person or thing one especially dislikes, a persistent irritant.

clue.text: A border flower planted in tin vessel

indicators.note: planted in means set inside, as a bulb goes in a pot

parts.note: a can is a tin
a flower is crossword-speak for a river; the Tamar forms the Devon and Cornwall border

explanation.surface: A gardener puts a border plant into a tin used as a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is something that flows, a river. The Tamar marks the boundary between the English counties of Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled boat, a kind of watercraft.

clue.text: Central point of female vanity — to get a reaction?

indicators.note: a reaction is read here as a re-action, a going back, so the letters run backwards
of means taken from within, so the letters sit across the words female vanity

parts.note: the middle of the body, often pierced or bared by vain women hoping to be noticed

explanation.surface: A woman's vain display of her midriff is meant to provoke a response.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue looks like a cryptic definition about belly-button display, but the letters sit backwards across 'female vanity'.
explanation.definitionFit: The navel of something is its hub or centre, as Delphi was called the navel of the world.

clue.text: Some of church really welcomed holy man

indicators.note: welcomed means taken in, so the holy man is received inside the other word

parts.note: really means very
St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A church congregation warmly welcomed a visiting holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it is the definition: a part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is a room in a church where clergy robe and vestments are kept, so it is part of the building.

clue.text: That man's after 20% off fast food

indicators.note: after places that man behind the trimmed word
off means taken away, so that fifth of the word is dropped from its end

parts.note: fast means quick
twenty per cent of a five-letter word is one letter, here its final one
that man is he; the apostrophe s is just is, a link

explanation.surface: Someone is chasing a 20% discount at a fast-food outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' reads as one phrase, but fast is wordplay and food alone defines. '20% off' removes one letter of five, the K.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury egg-and-cheese tart, an item one eats.

clue.text: Plant water covers Jimmy knocking back pint

indicators.note: covers means goes around, so the water's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
Jimmy Riddle is rhyming slang for piddle, so a jimmy is a wee

indicators.note: knocking back a drink reverses the abbreviation here

explanation.surface: A man called Jimmy knocks back a pint, then spills water over himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' looks like drinking but reverses PT to TP. Jimmy Riddle is British rhyming slang for piddle, i.e. urination.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing garden flower prized for its scent.

clue.text: Slip from terminal in Beijing with 50 yen

indicators.note: terminal means the final letter of the city name

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a yen is a longing or itch

explanation.surface: A flight from a Beijing terminal paid with fifty yen goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Yen looks like the Japanese currency, but here it means a craving.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a minor error or malfunction, a small slip.

clue.text: Egg-producer central to ornate colouring

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs

indicators.note: central to picks the two middle letters of the word ornate

explanation.surface: An egg-laying bird is central to some ornate decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye used on hair and skin, a colouring agent.

clue.text: Part of body first to deteriorate's inside joint

indicators.note: inside puts the letter within the joint's letters

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting part of a mortise-and-tenon woodwork joint

indicators.note: first to points to the opening letter of the word deteriorate

explanation.surface: An ageing body part is the first to deteriorate inside a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The body-joint picture misleads: the joint is the carpentry tenon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is the tough cord linking muscle to bone, an anatomical structure.

clue.text: Evergreen song by Abba, with computer technology replacing members

indicators.note: replacing tells us one set of letters is swapped out for another

parts.note: Mamma Mia is a hit song by the Swedish pop group Abba
members of parliament are MPs; M for member, twice, gives MM
CAD stands for computer-aided design

explanation.surface: An evergreen Abba hit is remade with computer technology replacing the band members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen' suggests a timeless song, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is an evergreen Australian tree grown for its nuts.

clue.text: Foreign letter ending used in present tense

parts.note: tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of the word present

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on a foreign letter's ending in the present tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present tense' reads as grammar, but tense alone is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means stretched tight or strained, as nerves or a rope can be.

clue.text: Make perfect heart in rhyme for beloved

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen or refine to perfection

indicators.note: heart in picks the central letter of the word rhyme

explanation.surface: A poet perfects the heart of a rhyme for a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey is a term of endearment for a loved one, a darling.

clue.text: Milk deliverer heading for excitement provided lady's around

indicators.note: around tells us the lady's letters go round the rest

parts.note: her is the possessive for a lady

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of the word excitement

parts.note: provided means if

explanation.surface: A milkman gets excited about a lady, provided she comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk deliverer' suggests a milkman; it is a young cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young cow, which yields milk once she calves.

clue.text: See you texting Rees regularly. Is it therapy?

definitions.note: a question form of remedy or treatment

parts.note: in text-speak see you is written CU

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the name Rees

explanation.surface: Someone texting a person named Rees wonders whether it is therapeutic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure is a remedy, a successful treatment.

clue.text: Fencing equipment safety mark covers point entering active torso

indicators.note: covers means goes around the rest

parts.note: the CE mark shows a product meets European safety standards

indicators.note: entering puts the point letter inside the rearranged torso letters
active means lively, so the letters of torso are rearranged

parts.note: E, for east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A fencer's kit carries a safety mark and covers the point entering the torso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' is the sport in the surface, but the fences are garden ones; 'active' signals the rearranging of the body word before the point goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is the tarry wood preservative painted onto garden fences.

clue.text: Pairs leading tackle high tides somewhere in the Pacific

indicators.note: pairs leading means the opening two letters of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Advice for sailors tackling high tides somewhere in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the main island of French Polynesia, in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Nursed former South American soldier

parts.note: the Incas were a pre-Columbian people of Peru
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier

explanation.surface: A former South American soldier was nursed back to health.
explanation.definitionFit: A child in care is looked after by the state, so the phrase means tended or looked after.

clue.text: Gutless affair with diva disgraced MP

indicators.note: gutless means with the insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: Cher is the American singer, a diva

explanation.surface: A disgraced MP's affair with a diva shows him to be gutless.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, novelist and former Conservative MP, was jailed for perjury.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist Jeffrey Archer, once a Member of Parliament, was later imprisoned for perjury.

clue.text: Old chestnut, tallest in copse, contracted skin disease

indicators.note: in a down entry the tallest, i.e. highest, letter of copse is its first
contracted means shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: lichen is a skin complaint with small papules

explanation.surface: The tallest tree in a copse, an old chestnut, has caught a skin disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old chestnut' looks like a tree in the copse, but means a stale joke.
explanation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a joke or saying worn out by repetition, an overused phrase.

clue.text: Scotch attracts Derry's most popular character. Paddy?

indicators.note: attracts means draws in, so the letter is pulled inside

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to stop it
R is the letter appearing most often in the word Derry

explanation.surface: Scotch whisky draws Derry's most popular figure, an Irishman nicknamed Paddy.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like an Irishman's name, but it is a fit of temper; the question mark admits the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is British slang for a fit of temper, a tantrum or sulk.

clue.text: In the UK/US etc, demo initially pruned political funds

indicators.note: in places the trimmed protest inside the region

parts.note: the West is the term for those Western nations

indicators.note: initially pruned means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: Western nations ran a demo that pruned their political funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is money set aside for a campaign, especially an election.

clue.text: Tramp starved, regularly lacking a vitamin

indicators.note: regularly lacking means every other letter of starved is dropped

parts.note: vitamin K helps blood to clot

explanation.surface: A starved tramp regularly lacks a vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tramp looks like a vagrant, but as a verb it means walk wearily.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or a long way, as on a trek.

clue.text: Take exam in university, laid back, unmoved

indicators.note: in puts the exam letters inside the turned word
laid back means turned backwards

parts.note: to sit an exam is to take it

explanation.surface: A laid-back student takes an exam at university, unmoved by stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' reads as relaxed but turns UNI to INU.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for in place, in situ means in the original position, not shifted.

clue.text: European capital formerly attracted second-class stars

indicators.note: attracted means drew in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the lira was the currency, or capital, of Italy before the euro
B is second class, after A

explanation.surface: A European capital once attracted second-rate celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city such as Rome, but means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is a constellation and sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Cricketer starts to hook unduly during fast century

indicators.note: during puts the letters inside the fasting period

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of hook and unduly

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, a century in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman starts to hook unduly during a fast century.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Len Hutton was a great England and Yorkshire batsman; a century, 100 runs, is called a ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Len Hutton was a celebrated English opening batsman who captained England.
